newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans names new stock exchange chief.
newsitem.headline: Caymans names new stock exchange chief.

text.p: Former Wall Street securities attorney David Carrad is to head the newly-created Cayman Islands Stock Exchange, the government announced.
During the past year Carrad served as legal advisor to the Cambodian Commerce Ministry helping to rebuild the country's legal system with regard to trade and commercial matters.
He comes to his new post through the International Securities Consultancy Company of Hong Kong, which is advising the Cayman government over the development of the exchange.

The bourse is expected to be on-line in late 1996 although no date has been set. It will concentrate on mutual funds listings and local stocks, but eventually international stocks, bonds and other securities will be listed.
There are 570 registered banks and trust institutions in the British territory with deposits in excess of $480 billion, according to government figures. (c) Reuters Limited 1996
